links.outcome: GPT-4 ADA ML model AUC and accuracy versus human specialist-developed reference models on same data
links.quote: ML strategies were valid and based on consistent coding routines, resulting in valid outputs on par with human specialist-developed reference models (AUC, 0.80 [95% CI: 0.80, 0.81] vs 0.80 [95% CI: 0.80, 0.81]; P = .51) (accuracy, 79% [6910 of 8758 patients] vs 78% [6875 of 8758 patients], respectively; P = .27).

links.outcome: Expert review of GPT-4 ADA outputs detecting statistical errors and inaccuracies
links.effect: Expert validation (methodology check, code quality, re-execution) found largely appropriate outputs but identified some statistical errors and inaccuracies.
links.quote: While GPT-4 ADA provided largely appropriate visualizations, descriptive statistical measures, quantitative statistical associations based on logistic regression, and gradient boosting machines for the predictive task (AUC, 0.75), some statistical errors and inaccuracies were encountered.

unlisted_practices: Expert validation of LLM autonomous data analysis code and statistical outputs (methodology, code quality, re-execution)

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates GPT-4 Advanced Data Analysis on automated statistical analysis and predictive modeling using a clinical chest radiograph dataset, validated by data scientists.
